cases.description: Render with Copier, name the repository homebrew-<tap>, configure Actions, and keep rendering separate from settings and secrets.
cases.prompt: Set up a new Homebrew tap for me from the template, and tell me what I need to configure. This is a desk exercise: do not edit anything, create a repository, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the template files and workflows you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Renders copier-homebrew-tap with Copier (copier copy), not a GitHub template repository, and commits .copier-answers.yml.
Says the repository must be named homebrew-<tap> so brew tap owner/tap resolves to it.
Lists Actions settings: keep default workflow permissions read-only and allow Actions to create and approve pull requests.
Treats creating the repository, changing settings or secrets, and pushing as steps that need the user's approval, separate from the local render.

cases.description: Explain which credentials exist, why update PRs have no bottles, and how bottles get published.
cases.prompt: Do I need a personal access token secret in the tap for the weekly updates, and why does an automated update PR not build bottles? How do bottles get published? This is a desk exercise: do not edit anything, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the template files and workflows you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Says the tap's update and dispatch workflows use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN and no update PAT or WORKFLOW_TOKEN secret is read, and that only an external producer dispatching to the tap needs its own token, stored in the producer.
Explains a PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger tests.yml, so update PRs have no bottle build until the PR is closed and reopened or pushed to.
Describes publishing as applying the pr-pull label, which runs publish.yml (brew pr-pull) after CI built the bottles.
Does not recommend a broad repo or admin token.

cases.description: Do not run copier update on a tap that has no answers file; adopt carefully.
cases.prompt: My existing tap was created from the old GitHub template repository. Can I just run copier update to get the latest template changes? This is a desk exercise: do not edit anything, create a repository, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the template files and workflows you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Says copier update needs .copier-answers.yml, which the tap does not have, so it cannot be run as is.
Proposes rendering the template to a scratch directory with matching answers, comparing file by file, and bringing over only approved changes while keeping formulae, casks and README prose.
Treats the adoption as a separate reviewed change and does not overwrite the tap blindly.
